name: shot_2_carl_illegal
prompt: Carl, a friendly green alligator butler in a black tuxedo with white shirt, vest and black bow tie, hangs upside down outside the balcony and drops suddenly into frame. He holds his silver serving tray perfectly steady, with the cloche, the drink and the white service napkin. Carl looks directly at the seated vacationer with a charming, offended smirk and clearly says: "That's illegal in Southwest Florida." He delivers the line with classy disbelief, like a butler politely correcting an outrageous mistake, his mouth movement synced naturally to the exact words. The vacationer stays seated in the white plastic chair and looks up in confused surprise. Setting: a Southwest Florida condo balcony at golden hour, turquoise Gulf water, beach, palm trees, orange-pink sunset, balcony railing, glass patio table with a phone, sunglasses and a half-finished drink. Look: realistic 35mm tropical social-ad film, warm Kodak-style grain, shallow depth of field, golden-hour glow, humid Florida air, soft ocean sparkle, palm shadows, natural cinematic lighting. Carl is a premium animated-real mascot integrated into the real balcony environment. Camera: one move only, a subtle handheld push-in toward Carl and the seated vacationer, natural and premium, not shaky. Audio: the spoken line plus light ambient ocean breeze only, no music. Acting is funny, polished and controlled; Carl is magical, confident and slightly mischievous, never scary.
